plain_english: Then, having overcome power, the mantras—possessing the power of the omniscient—proceed for authority, like instruments of embodied beings.
sanskrit_cite: tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ pravartante adhikārāya karaṇānīva iva dehinām

plain_english: There only they dissolve, peaceful and stainless, together with the worshipper's mind; by that they become Śiva-natured.
sanskrit_cite: tatraiva saṃpralīyante śāntarūpāḥ nirañjanāḥ saha ārādhakacittena tena te śivadharmiṇaḥ

plain_english: Because the individual soul is all-pervading, from the arising of all states, by the form of that experience and by realization of identity.
sanskrit_cite: yasmāt sarvamayaḥ jīvaḥ sarvabhāvasamudbhavāt tatsaṃvedanarūpeṇa tādātmyapratipattitaḥ

plain_english: Therefore that is not a state in thoughts of word and meaning; Śiva, the experiencer, is indeed always situated everywhere as object of enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: tena śabdārthacintāsu na sā avasthā na yaḥ śivaḥ bhoktā eva bhogyabhāvena sadā sarvatra saṃsthitaḥ

plain_english: He, seeing constantly and united, is liberated while living; there is no doubt.
sanskrit_cite: sa paśyan satataṃ yuktaḥ jīvanmuktaḥ na saṃśayaḥ

plain_english: This indeed is the rising of that to-be-meditated in the meditator's mind: absorption in that selfhood, which the desiring practitioner has.
sanskrit_cite: ayam eva udayaḥ tasya dhyeyasya dhyāyicetasi tadātmatāsamāpattiḥ icchataḥ sādhakasya yā

plain_english: This indeed is attainment of immortality; this indeed is grasping of the self; and this is initiation into liberation, bestowing Śiva-existence.
sanskrit_cite: iyam eva amṛtaprāptiḥ ayam eva ātmanaḥ grahaḥ iyam nirvāṇadīkṣā ca śivasadbhāvadāyinī

plain_english: As desire is requested, the creator, of waking, makes objects situated in the heart and the rising of moon and sun, and accomplishes them for the embodied.
sanskrit_cite: yathā icchā abhyarthitaḥ dhātā jāgrataḥ arthān hṛdisthitān somasūryodayaṃ kṛtvā saṃpādayati dehinaḥ

plain_english: So also in dream, by not transgressing affection, one situated in the middle would always manifest desired objects more clearly.
sanskrit_cite: tathā svapne api abhīṣṭārthān praṇayasya anatikramāt nityaṃ sphuṭataraṃ madhye sthitaḥ prakāśayet

plain_english: Otherwise creation would be independent, due to having that nature, always like the worldly in the two states of waking and dream.
sanskrit_cite: anyathā tu svatantrā syāt sṛṣṭiḥ taddharmakatvataḥ satataṃ laukikasya iva jāgratsvapnapadadvaye

plain_english: As indeed an object seen unclear even in an attentive mind shines again clearer, cultivated by one's own power and effort.
sanskrit_cite: yathā hi arthaḥ asphuṭaḥ dṛṣṭaḥ sāvadhāne api cetasi bhūyaḥ sphuṭataraḥ bhāti svabalodyogabhāvitaḥ

plain_english: So whatever is situated in ultimate sense, when, where, and how, having overcome power, it proceeds not after long.
sanskrit_cite: tathā yat paramārthena yadā yatra yathā sthitam tat tathā balam ākramya na cirāt saṃpravartate

plain_english: Even a weak one, having overcome that, proceeds in action; because one would cover hunger, so one very hungry.
sanskrit_cite: durbalaḥ api tadākramya yataḥ kārye pravartate ācchādayet bubhukṣāṃ ca tathā yaḥ atibubhukṣitaḥ
